creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Follow on from `make-interaction` (a_25Rcu1uOI), which shipped `--reply`/`--reply-na`. Found by adversarially probing that feature; every case below reproduced against v0.11.0.

`--reply` keys answers by line number, so several semantically different questions that funnel through one `input()` all share a key:

```rad
fn ask(label):
    return input("Enter {label}: ")   // line 7 - the only prompt site

host = ask("hostname")                // line 9
user = ask("username")                // line 10
port = ask("port")                    // line 11
```

RAD20046 reports the site once, and says nothing about what it asks or how often:

```
04_helper.rad:7  input may run more than once - repeat --reply per run
```

Answers bind in execution order, confirmed with marker values:

```
--reply 7:FIRST --reply 7:SECOND --reply 7:THIRD
  -> host=FIRST  user=SECOND  port=THIRD
```

So nothing swaps inside rad. The caller simply has no way to learn the order is host, user, port. Reading it as username-first and passing `alice, db.internal, 5432` gives `db.internal@alice:5432` and exit 0. Every value is free text, so nothing downstream can catch it.

RAD20046 *does* print prompt text when it's a literal (`08_retry.rad:8  input "Environment? "`). It drops it here because `"Enter {label}: "` is interpolated - the case where the reader most needs it.

### Direction

The key names a position, not a question. Options, roughly cheapest first:

- Print the raw template even when interpolated. `input "Enter {label}: "` at least shows the question varies per pass.
- List call sites alongside the definition. Static analysis already resolves them: `input at :7, reached from :9, :10, :11`.
- An opt-in stable id - `input("Enter {label}: ", id="host")` answered by `--reply host:db.internal`. Order-independent and survives refactors, at the cost of a new named arg on four functions.

The last also covers the reorder case: swapping two adjacent `input()` calls silently rebinds a saved command, because rad validates *that* a line prompts and never *what* it asks. That one is parked, but it shares this root cause and is worth weighing when choosing here.
title: Prompts inside a helper function share one --reply key and bind by order
